figures.finding: Minors (under eighteen) are legally incapable of contracting except where the Code allows; the incapacity can be pleaded for the minor but not against him; simple lesion annuls any act of an unmarried minor not aided by his tutor, but a minor who is a trader or mechanic can't be relieved from contracts made for his business, and one who ratifies after majority can't be relieved. So a minor's contract for performing or creative work binds when his tutor aids or makes it (reading); no earnings set-aside rule was found.

value.binding: the tutor's aid (Civil Code, causes of nullity)

figures.applies: Civil Code of Saint Lucia (Revised Laws 2023), arts. 213, 284 and the chapter on contracts.

sources.said: 213. Persons of either sex remain in minority until they attain the full age of 18 years.

(1) Those legally incapable of contracting are:— (a) minors except in the special cases described in this Code; ... The incapacity of a minor and of an interdicted person may, when the contract is not by this Code declared to be void, be pleaded by or for him or her but not against him or her.

Simple lesion is a cause of nullity in favour of an unmarried minor against every kind of act when not aided by his tutor, ... A minor who is a banker, trader or mechanic is not relievable for cause of lesion from contracts made for the purposes of his or her business or trade. ... A person is not relievable from a contract made by him or her during minority, when he or she has ratified it since attaining the age of majority.

figures.finding: No child under the school-leaving age may be employed save in light work in school holidays, but the bar doesn't reach work by children or young persons in artistic performances under a permit the Minister grants in his discretion case by case, limiting the hours to be worked and stating the conditions of work; nor may a child or young person do work that puts at risk his well-being, education, safety, health or development. A young person (over fifteen, under eighteen) needs a doctor's certificate of fitness and yearly medical supervision. The permit is for 'artistic performances', which reads as performing; a child writer or director isn't named (reading).

value.permit: permit granted by the Minister responsible for Labour, case by case

sources.said: 122.— (1) Notwithstanding section 18 (2) and subject to subsection (2), a person shall not employ or allow to be employed any child who is under the minimum school leaving age as declared by any law in force in Saint Lucia except for employment during school holidays in light work. ... (g) work done by children or young persons participating in artistic performances based on a permit granted by the Minister in his or her discretion on a case by case basis limiting hours to be worked and indicating conditions of work. ... 123. A young person shall not be employed or allowed to be employed unless he or she has been certified as fit and suitable for the work which he or she is expected to perform by a medical practitioner after a medical examination and thereafter his or her employment shall be subject to annual medical supervision

figures.finding: No one under eighteen may form or join in forming a company, and anyone so barred may not be a director.

sources.said: (2) An individual shall not form or join in the formation of a company under this Act who — (a) is less than 18 years of age;
(1) An individual who is prohibited by section 4(2) from forming or joining in the formation of a company may not be a director of any company.
